advances: The inequalities concern summed intrinsic mass in a single selected same-parity set and include actual closed caps. The sharpness example concerns the mass coefficient.

proof:
The positive selected fibers have a common $q$-dimensional direction $L$. For each pair, convexity contains its midpoint body in the actual integer midpoint fiber, whose dimension is at most $q$. The direction of the midpoint body is the sum of the input directions and hence forces them to coincide. Any anchored combination of selected fibers at a selected base is contained in that actual fiber. Orthogonal projection onto $L$ is an isometry on each corresponding affine plane, so Brunn–Minkowski gives $w_p^{1/q}\ge\sum_i\alpha_iw_{p_i}^{1/q}$ for every anchored representation $p=\sum_i\alpha_i p_i$. The same reasoning gives the displayed root lower bound on each edge midpoint fiber.

Define the roof at $x\in\operatorname{conv}P$ as the largest $\sum_i\alpha_iw_{p_i}^{1/q}$ over convex representations of $x$ by $P$. The maximum exists on the compact coefficient polytope, equals the datum at each $p\in P$, and is concave by combining representations. The upper boundary of the finite lifted polytope gives a polytopal subdivision of $\operatorname{conv}P$ on which this roof is affine. If the roof is globally affine the one cell suffices. Pull each cell with a single common vertex order. Pulling recursively cones the triangulations of facets that omit the first vertex to that vertex and restricts to the pulling triangulation on every face, so the cells fit together. Insert each remaining base from $P$ by subdividing the unique simplex whose relative interior contains it, coning its boundary to the new point, and replacing that face by its subdivision in every incident simplex. These stellar subdivisions are compatible and refine existing affine pieces. The resulting vertex set is exactly $P$, and each vertex lies in an $s$-simplex, giving degree at least $s$.

The set of maximizers of the roof is convex and is triangulated by the faces spanned by maximum-height vertices. Its graph is connected, since a segment in that set connects any two vertices through a finite chain of incident simplices. From any other vertex the segment toward a maximizing vertex initially lies in a simplex incident to the starting vertex and increases the roof by concavity. Roof affinity on that simplex gives a strictly higher neighbor. Choose one such edge toward a parent at every nonmaximum vertex, and root a spanning tree of the maximum subgraph at $p_*$. Every vertex reaches the root, so the chosen edges form the claimed tree.

Each edge midpoint is integral and lies in the relative interior of its edge. Those interiors are disjoint from the vertices and from one another. Summing the separately forced midpoint volumes therefore gives the first inequality. Write $\delta=2^{-q}$. On a tree edge from parent volume $b$ to child volume $c\le b$, the binomial bound is $\delta b+(1-\delta)c$ because every term except the pure $b$ term is at least its coefficient times $c$. On each other edge the two pure terms give $\delta(w_p+w_{p'})$. Summing the child baseline gives $M_P-a$. After removing it, the root gets one positive coefficient in the $\delta$ bracket from every incident edge. Each other vertex gets one negative coefficient from its parent edge and positive ones from all other incident edges. This proves the graph inequality. The minimum degree gives the stated excess for $s\ge2$. In rank one the triangulation is a path with endpoints of degree one and other vertices of degree two, giving the two expressions in the statement. Rank zero is a singleton.

For sharpness fix $s\ge2$, take a unit-volume $q$-body $K$ containing zero, and prescribe over $2\Delta_s$ the homothetic fibers $r(z)K$, with $r(z)=1-(1-\epsilon)\sum_i z_i/2$ and $0<\epsilon<1$. This is a convex body in the $s+q$ active coordinates because $r$ is positive affine and weighted Minkowski sums of positive homothetic copies equal the copy at the weighted scale. If additional base coordinates are desired, thicken by intervals with zero as their only integer point. For $d>q$, embed the construction in a fixed continuous $q$-plane, which is allowed for compact convex $E$.

The all-even sites have volumes $1,b,\ldots,b$ with $b=\epsilon^q$. The only other sites are $e_i$ with $c=((1+\epsilon)/2)^q$ and $e_i+e_j$ with volume $b$. Thus the exact slack is $s(c-b)+\binom{s}{2}b\to s2^{-q}$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. The cap version follows by applying the argument to the compact convex set $C\cap H$ itself, so it includes all sampled boundary fibers of the closed cap and does not alter the lattice.
statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, and let $q\ge1$ be the largest dimension of any nonempty integer fiber. Write $M$ for the total intrinsic $\mathcal H_q$ mass of its integer trace. For any nonempty set $P$ of bases of positive $q$-volume in one parity class put $w_p=\mathcal H_q(E_p)$, $M_P=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$, $a=\max_{p\in P}w_p$, and $s=\dim\operatorname{aff}P$. There is a triangulation graph $G$ with vertex set exactly $P$ and a root $p_*$ with $w_{p_*}=a$ such that
$$
\begin{aligned}
M&\ge M_P+\sum_{\{p,p'\}\in G}\left(\frac{w_p^{1/q}+w_{p'}^{1/q}}2\right)^q\\
 &\ge 2M_P-a+2^{-q}\left[\deg_G(p_*)a+\sum_{p\ne p_*}(\deg_G(p)-2)w_p\right].
\end{aligned}
$$
The triangulation makes the concave roof of the input volume roots affine on its simplices, and has a spanning tree ascending in volume toward $p_*$. For $s\ge2$ the excess above $2M_P-a$ is at least $2^{-q}[(s-2)M_P+2a]\ge s2^{-q}a$. The coefficient $s2^{-q}$ relative to $a$ is optimal for each $s\ge2$ and $q\ge1$. When $s=1$ the bracket is $a$ minus the opposite endpoint volume if the root is an endpoint, or twice $a$ minus the sum of endpoint volumes otherwise. For $s=0$, $M\ge a$. The theorem includes $q=d$ and every actual closed cap $E=C\cap H$, with the largest dimension and mass taken within $E$.
title: A parity triangulation gives a sharp quantitative rank gain
